concepts.def: Central declaration: 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One' (Deuteronomy 6:4); recited twice daily.
Sacred agreement between God and Jewish people; Abraham (Genesis 17) and Moses at Sinai (Exodus 19-24); Torah obligations.
613 commandments in the Torah: 248 positive, 365 negative; foundation of halakhic Jewish life.
Anointed king from David's line who will restore Israel and bring peace; debate within Judaism on identity.
Repairing the world; concept of Jews' duty to perfect imperfect creation through ethical action and social justice.
Principle that saving a life overrides almost all Torah commandments; even Sabbath can be broken to save someone.

Judaism: The Prophets — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Judaism: The Prophets brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Judaism: The Prophets.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
